title: Drawdown: staying in the game
desc: Measure a drawdown and size for the worst fall

cards.title: Back to even
cards.situation: Your $10,000 portfolio falls 50% to $5,000. What gain do you need to get back to $10,000?

visual.title: Down and back
visual.label: $10,000 falls to $5,000; what gain gets it back to $10,000?

options.feedback: The gain works on a smaller pot. 50% of $5,000 is only $2,500.
A 50% loss needs a 100% gain. Losses hurt more than gains help.
Closer, but 75% of $5,000 is $3,750. You need $5,000 more: the whole pot again.

cards.added: Feedback for C written for the Academy

cards.title: Drawdown
cards.text: A **[[drawdown|drawdown]]** is the fall from a peak to the lowest point after it. It’s the pain you have to sit through.

visual.title: Your portfolio
visual.label: The portfolio peaks at $12,000 and falls to a low of $8,400, a 30% drawdown

blocks.tip: $12,000 → $8,400 = −30%. Broad stock markets have fallen 50% or more in their worst crashes.

cards.title: The recovery math
cards.text: The deeper the fall, the bigger the climb back. And it grows fast.

visual.label: A 10% fall needs 11% to recover, 20% needs 25%, 30% needs 43%, 50% needs 100%

cards.foot: Small falls are easy to repair. Deep ones can take years, so avoiding them matters most.
cards.added: Board label “tap a row”: built as ▶ Play on the hbars (hbars rows aren’t tappable)

cards.title: Size for the worst
cards.text: You have $100,000. Picture stocks falling 50%, as they have in big crashes. Assume bonds and cash hold steady.

visual.label: In a 50% stock crash an 80/20 mix loses $40,000 and a 40/60 mix loses $20,000

cards.rule: if that fall would make you sell at the bottom, you hold too much risk.

cards.title: Find the drawdown
cards.q: Your portfolio peaked at $40,000, fell to $30,000, and is now back at $36,000. What was the drawdown?

options.feedback: That’s the gap between the peak and today. A drawdown runs from the peak to the low.
A drawdown is measured from the peak, not from the low.
Too big. The fall was $10,000, measured against the $40,000 peak.

cards.added: Feedback for the options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy

cards.title: Why size for drawdowns?
cards.q: What’s the main reason to size your portfolio for a big drawdown?

options.feedback: No portfolio avoids every loss. The goal is a fall you can live through, so you stay in for the recovery.

options.text: So you can sit through the worst and not sell at the bottom
options.feedback: A fall you can live through keeps you in for the recovery.
Sizing for drawdowns is about surviving the fall, not boosting returns.
Fees are a separate cost. Sizing is about a fall you can sit through.

cards.headline: You can plan to stay in the game.
lines: Drawdown: the fall from peak to low.
A 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover.
Size for the worst fall you could live through.
